speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. To begin our limited inquiry, can you tell me if you have any history of chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) or a known genetic condition like Friedreich's ataxia?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. Since you are experiencing ataxia and clumsiness, specifically more pronounced on the right side, have you noticed any involuntary movements in your limbs, or has your balance been affected since childhood?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain showing cerebellar abnormalities. Given your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, we must urgently rule out Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), which can present with ataxia and gait disturbance.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Patient
text: The walking difficulty and coordination problems are the main issues. I do not have chest pain or other major symptoms besides the neurological problems. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.
